title: Pre/in/post-order traversal shapes
description: Three recursive tree-traversal shapes side-by-side — only the position of visit(n) moves between them.

notes: Inorder on a BST yields values in sorted ascending order — that is the one-line BST invariant.
Preorder visits root before children — natural for serialize/clone (you have the root before recursing).
Postorder visits children before root — natural for bottom-up aggregation (subtree sum, height, safe delete).
All three are O(n) time and O(h) recursion-stack space — only the visit position differs.

questions.q: Which traversal yields a BST's values in sorted ascending order?
questions.explain: BST invariant: left < node < right. Visiting in left -> node -> right order emits sorted output.

questions.q: In preorder traversal, when is the current node visited relative to its children?
Postorder traversal is the natural choice for which task?
options: Scanning a BST in sorted order
Bottom-up aggregation like subtree sum or safe delete
Finding the shortest path between two nodes
questions.explain: Postorder finishes both children before the parent, so you have child results ready when you visit the parent.

questions.q: Across all three traversals, what changes between them?
questions.explain: Left-then-right order is identical; only where visit(n) sits relative to the two recursive calls changes.

questions.q: Which traversal is the natural choice for serializing a tree so it can be rebuilt by reading nodes in order?
options: preorder — you emit the root before its subtrees, so deserialization knows the parent before its children
inorder — sorted output rebuilds the tree
postorder — children-first is easiest to rebuild
Any of them work identically for serialization
questions.explain: Preorder emits root-first, so a recursive deserializer reads the parent, then reconstructs left then right subtrees — inorder alone is ambiguous for reconstruction.

questions.q: What is the time and recursion-stack space cost of any of these traversals on a tree of n nodes with height h?
options: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
questions.explain: Every node is visited once → O(n) time; the call stack only holds the current root-to-node path → O(h), which is O(log n) for balanced and O(n) for a degenerate (linked-list) tree.

questions.q: To write an ITERATIVE traversal that mimics the recursion, which auxiliary structure replaces the call stack?
questions.explain: Recursion uses the call stack (LIFO), so an iterative version pushes/pops an explicit stack; using a queue instead would give level-order (BFS), not a depth-first traversal.

exercises.prompt: Fill in inorder traversal — recurse LEFT, visit, recurse RIGHT.
Fill in preorder AND postorder. Only the position of out.push(n.val) differs.

L3.prompt: Given the BST { val:2, left:{val:1,...}, right:{val:3,...} }, log its values in inorder — one console.log per value. Expected: 1, then 2, then 3 on separate lines.
hints: Recurse left, log the current node's value, recurse right.
Base case: if (!n) return — null children are no-ops.
